entry.description: Chooses an option the passage explicitly denies, rather than one it merely fails to support. Distinguished from a plausible option the passage never states: here the passage states the contrary. Negation-dropped loses a WORD; this loses a CLAIM, and the option may share no wording with the line that refutes it.
entry.childHint: One line in the passage says something different. Go back and find it.

stem.text: Read lines 56 to 62. The Mole says, 'Oh, it’s all very well to talk.' What does this show about him?

carriers.key: He did not know how anyone could get across the river.

options.value: He did not know how anyone could get across the river.
He thought the Water Rat was being unkind to him.
He did not want to be friends with the Water Rat.
He was too tired from his walk to move.
He knew all about boats but did not own one.
options.execution: Line 62 says he 'did not yet fully understand its uses', which contradicts knowing all about boats.

stem.text: Read lines 66 to 67. What does the last thing the Mole says show about his day?

carriers.key: The whole day had been full of things he had never done before.

options.value: He was hoping the Rat would let him hold the oars.
He was still frightened of the water.
The whole day had been full of things he had never done before.
He was already wishing he was back in his own house.
options.execution: Nothing says he wants to go home; line 66 has him calling it a wonderful day.

options.value: He had been in boats before, but never one as fine as this.

stem.text: Look at lines 5 to 8. What can Priya see from where she is standing?

carriers.key: A gap under the roof where two boards have parted.

options.value: The flagstone beside the water butt.
A gap under the roof where two boards have parted.
A grey nest hanging under the roof board.
So many going in that she cannot keep count.
options.execution: Line 7 has her eyes doing the counting without being asked.

stem.text: Look at lines 21 and 22 and lines 48 to 50. What do the two moments show about Priya and the nest?

carriers.key: She kept them to herself, and now she says out loud that they are hers.

options.value: She told nobody about them, and she has two fists in his sleeve at the door.
She kept them to herself, and now she says out loud that they are hers.
She had already told her mother about them before this morning.
She speaks so that Grandad will not be stung by them.

stem.text: Look at lines 34 to 36. How has the traffic under the boards changed?

carriers.key: More are out, and they are circling one patch of air.

options.value: More are out, and they are circling one patch of air.
The traffic under the boards has changed.
Priya is looking past his shoulder.
They have moved away from the roofline altogether.
options.execution: Line 36 keeps them above the guttering.

stem.text: Think about the whole passage. How does the writer handle the thing in the shed?

carriers.key: We are shown them over and over, but the writer never names them.

options.value: The wall hummed against her ear, and the nest hung under the board.
Priya knows what they are, but she has not yet worked out where they live.
options.execution: Line 20 has her see the nest itself through the gap.

options.value: We are told what they are, and then shown them again and again.
